column4: git log -- <path> hides a merge that took one parent's version of a file whole, so a develop head can carry an older kernel than the feature commits in its own history: the align commit 94486a51a24 reset synexia-mat-collections/native/mat_posting_merge.c to its 2026-11-02 blob (781288b369, no galloping, no count kernels) while the develop Java declares seven natives; the complete kernel (9f301002dc, 572 lines, commit 7a309c659e7) sits in the same tree under m3/qualification/master-landing-20261028/retained-variants/pr15528/. Read git log --full-history and --stat of the feature commits before pinning a donor blob
column5: git log --full-history shows 20+ superset merges touching the C; blob table: FETCH_HEAD 781288b369 (3 symbols) vs 7a309c659e7 9f301002dc (7 symbols); git show --stat 94486a51a24 lists both paths

column4: the Java owner needed its donor closure (MatSelection -> MatBits, MatIntList) and the plan's "java.util.BitSet bridge" would have been a hand-written production class, which the Chrome generation rule holds when Chrome is down; relocating the closure by recipe (M3IntSelection, M3SelectionBits, M3IntPostingList) keeps every production body a pinned donor body.
